name: Live Events Production

stations.why: The company switch tie-in: cam-locks ground first, and the phase check before anything is energised.
Loading a lineset, where an unbalanced arbor is a runaway with a person on the rope.
Points overhead, with automation cues proven before the house is let in.
Motors: inspection, capacity and never leaving a load hanging on a brake.
The arena load-in from the deck: truss inspected and spliced, flown level on its motors with nobody under it, and every point dead-hung on its steel.
A spot tower before doors: the lift ridden held, the tower anchor clipped before the gate opens, a cracked coupler caught, and the lamp struck from its own switch clear of the housing.
The front-of-house rail before doors: a bent pin caught, the line built and gauged to the plan, and the show-stop chain briefed and used when the load gauge spikes.

summary: A load-in from the truck to the house lights, in the order a call actually runs, with the two things that kill on a stage: what is overhead and what is energised.
union: IATSE — International Alliance of Theatrical Stage Employees
